To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the place of a foundling room is produced and maintained by the care infrastructures that are bound to it, and that these infrastructures allow the place to be a place-by-proxy, which in turn allows for its animation by the people that use it.

(1) places are not simply ‘there’ but are continuously produced through care infrastructures; (2) places are not bounded entities, but rather are open and permeable; (3) places can be understood as ‘place-by-proxies’ that allow for the animation of care infrastructures around them; and (4) the concept of place can be fruitfully applied to sociological investigations into care and health architectures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the materialities of care infrastructures in healthcare and the ways these infrastructures shape the experience of care.
the ways in which care infrastructures produce and sustain place, and how place, in turn, produces and sustains care infrastructures.
the ways in which places, and the materialities that produce them, are implicated in the production of care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
place-by-proxy is a place where the care of a baby is enabled by a care infrastructure, where the place is not the care infrastructure itself but is the result of the work of care.
the concept of place-by-proxy can be used as an analytical tool for the study of care infrastructures in healthcare and other social settings.
this article is a good example of how the concept of place-by-proxy can be used in a variety of sociological research fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
place-by-proxy is a concept that allows for an understanding of the material and social processes that make places of care, and care infrastructures, possible.
place is a sociological concept that can be fruitfully employed to understand the materialities that make up ecologies of care.
place, in the form of place-by-proxy, is a powerful tool for sociologists of healthcare to understand how care infrastructures are organized, maintained, and changed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of place-by-proxy allows for a better conceptualization and analysis of care and healthcare infrastructures.
place-by-proxy is not only a place, but also an assemblage of materialities, people and practices that are brought into place by the care infrastructures that sustain them.
place is not only a social and cultural construct, but also a material and ecological phenomenon.
